questions.ask: Which C do we keep in the logo: the needle's eye or the stitch?
questions.why: You asked for one custom detail on the C only, tied to the copper thread. Two versions passed design review. The needle's eye: a small slot cut into the thick left stroke of the C, and the copper thread passes through it, so the C itself becomes the needle. The stitch: five small stitch holes along the outer edge of the C, like a seam. The V and everything else stay as you saw them. Picture: evidence/logo/c-options.png (current logo top left, then both options, each also at 32 and 64 px). Your pick then goes into the wordmark and the dark-background versions; the tiny favicon keeps the plain C, because both details close up at that size.

options.label: Needle's eye
options.detail: The thread visibly goes through the C. The reviewer's pick: one clear idea, reads as made to measure

options.label: Stitch
options.detail: A seam along the C's edge; echoes the stitch in the Text Draft, but white holes on black can look like a stock leather-patch effect

options.label: Neither, keep the plain C
options.detail: Keep the faithful redraw as it is

feedback.title: A task can follow only one follow-up item
feedback.body: Two open follow-up items (a decision to remove old concepts and an unfinished housekeeping task) belonged naturally to one housekeeping task, but a task takes a single follow_up ref, so the plan was refused until the task was split in two. Accepting a list of follow-up refs per task would keep the plan shaped like the work.
